units.zh: 《傳》曰：「王者功成作樂，治定制禮。」
units.en: The Classic says: "When a true king has completed his great work, he composes music; when governance is settled, he establishes ritual."
units.literal: The Classic says: "When a true king has achieved his meritorious work, he creates music; when order is established, he fixes ritual."

units.en: Surely this is no mere ornamental excess of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!
units.literal: Surely this is no mere superfluous flourish of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!

units.zh: 蓋有天下者，將一軌度、正民俗、合人神、和上下，舍禮樂何以焉。
units.en: Whoever holds the realm must unify standards, set custom right, join spirits and humans, and harmonize high and low — without ritual and music, how could any of this be achieved?
units.literal: For those who possess the realm must unify standards, rectify custom, harmonize spirits and humans and upper and lower — apart from ritual and music, how could this be done?

units.zh: 金初得宋，始有金石之樂，然而未盡其美也。
units.en: When the Jin first conquered the Song, they acquired bell-and-chime music for the first time, but its full refinement was still lacking.
units.literal: When the Jin first obtained the Song, they first had metal-and-stone music, yet they had not yet attained its full excellence.

units.zh: 及乎大定、明昌之際，日修月葺，粲然大備。
units.en: By the Dading and Mingchang eras, the court refined the system day by day and month by month until the musical establishment stood complete in splendid array.
units.literal: By the time of the Dading and Mingchang reigns, day by day they repaired and month by month they restored it, until it shone forth in full completeness.

units.zh: 其隸太常者，即郊廟、祀享、大宴、大朝會宮縣二舞是也。
units.en: Music under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices comprised the palace ensemble and the two ritual dances used at suburban and temple sacrifices, sacrificial offerings, great banquets, and major court assemblies.
units.literal: That which was subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was precisely the palace ensemble and the two dances for suburban and temple sacrifices, sacrificial offerings, great banquets, and great court assemblies.

units.zh: 隸教坊者，則有鐃歌鼓吹，天子行幸鹵簿導引之樂也。
units.en: The Music Bureau oversaw gong songs and wind-and-drum ensembles — the music that led the imperial procession whenever the Son of Heaven traveled.
units.literal: That subordinate to the Music Bureau had gong songs and wind-and-drum music — the music that guided the emperor's procession when he went on tour.

units.en: There was also variety music.
units.literal: There was variety music.

units.en: There was Bohai music as well.
units.literal: There was Bohai music.

units.zh: 有本國舊音，世宗嘗寫其意度為雅曲，史錄其一，其俚者弗載雲。
units.en: There were also the old melodies of the Jin homeland. Emperor Shizong once transcribed their modes into formal court music; the histories preserve one such piece, while vulgar tunes were deliberately left unrecorded.
units.literal: There were the old melodies of the native state; Emperor Shizong once set down their modes as formal music, and the histories record one of them; the vulgar ones are not recorded, it is said.

units.zh: 凡大祀、中祀、天子受冊寶、禦樓肆赦、受外國使賀則用之。
units.en: It was used for great sacrifices, middling sacrifices, the Son of Heaven's reception of the seal and treasure, imperial-balcony amnesties, and audiences for congratulatory envoys from foreign states.
units.literal: For great sacrifices, middling sacrifices, the Son of Heaven receiving the seal and treasure, imperial-balcony amnesty, and receiving congratulations from foreign envoys, it was used.

units.zh: 初，太宗取汴，得宋之儀章鐘磬樂虡，挈之以歸。
units.en: At the outset, when Emperor Taizong took Bian, he seized the Song court's ritual instruments, bells, chimes, and music stands and carried them back.
units.literal: At the beginning, when Emperor Taizong took Bian, he obtained the Song's ritual instruments, bells, chimes, and music stands, and carried them back.

units.zh: 皇統元年，熙宗加尊號，始就用宋樂，有司以鐘磬刻「晟」字者犯太宗諱，皆以黃紙封之。
units.en: In Huangtong 1, when Emperor Xizong received an elevated honorific title, the court first began to use Song music; officials found that bells and chimes engraved with the character "Sheng" violated Emperor Taizong's taboo, and all were sealed with yellow paper.
units.literal: In Huangtong 1, when Emperor Xizong received an elevated honorific title, they first began to use Song music; officials found that bells and chimes engraved with the character "Sheng" violated Emperor Taizong's taboo, and all were sealed with yellow paper.

units.zh: 大定十四年，太常始議：「歷代之樂各自為名，今郊廟社稷所用宋樂器犯廟諱，宜皆刮去，更為制名。」
units.en: In Dading 14, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices first reported: "The music of each dynasty has borne its own name; now the Song instruments used at suburban sacrifice, temple, and state-altar rites violate ancestral-taboo names and should all be scraped away and given new regulated names."
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dading, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices first deliberated: "The music of each dynasty has borne its own name; now the Song instruments used at suburban sacrifice, temple, and state-altar rites violate taboos of the ancestral temple and should all be scraped away and given new regulated names."

units.zh: 於是，命禮部、學士院、太常寺撰名，乃取大樂與天地同和之義，名之曰「太和」。
units.en: Thereupon he ordered the Ministry of Rites, the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to compose names, and taking the meaning that great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth, named it "Great Harmony."
units.literal: Thereupon he ordered the Ministry of Rites, the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to compose names, and taking the meaning that great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth, named it "Great Harmony."

units.en: There were the civil and military dances.
units.literal: There were the civil and military two dances.

units.zh: 皇統年間，定文舞曰《仁豐道洽之舞》，武舞曰《功成治定之舞》。
units.en: During the Huangtong era, the civil dance was fixed as "Dance of Benevolent Abundance and the Way Realized," and the military dance as "Dance of Merit Achieved and Order Settled."
units.literal: During the Huangtong era, the civil dance was fixed as "Dance of Benevolent Abundance and the Way Realized," and the military dance as "Dance of Merit Achieved and Order Settled."

units.zh: 《貞元儀》又改文舞曰《保大定功之舞》，武舞曰《萬國來同之舞》。
units.en: The Zhenyuan Yi again changed the civil dance to "Dance of Preserving Greatness and Establishing Merit," and the military dance to "Dance of the Ten Thousand States Coming in Unity."
units.literal: The Zhenyuan Yi again changed the civil dance to "Dance of Preserving Greatness and Establishing Merit," and the military dance to "Dance of the Ten Thousand States Coming in Unity."

units.zh: 大定十一年又有《四海會同之舞》，於是一代之制始備。
units.en: In Dading 11 there was added "Dance of the Four Seas Meeting in Unity," and with that the regulations of a single dynasty were for the first time complete.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading there was added "Dance of the Four Seas Meeting in Unity," and thus the regulations of one dynasty were for the first time complete.

units.zh: 明昌五年，詔用唐、宋故事，置所，講議禮樂。
units.en: In the fifth year of Mingchang, the court decreed that Tang and Song precedents be followed, established an office, and convened discussions on ritual and music.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, an edict ordered that Tang and Song precedents be followed, an office was established, and ritual and music were discussed.

units.zh: 有司謂：「雅樂自周、漢以來止存大法，魏、晉而後更造律度，訖無定論。
units.en: The responsible officials reported: "From Zhou and Han onward, formal music preserved only the broad principles; after Wei and Jin, courts repeatedly remade pitch standards, yet no lasting consensus was ever reached.
units.literal: The responsible officials said: "From Zhou and Han onward formal music preserved only the great principles; after Wei and Jin they repeatedly remade pitch standards, yet no final conclusion was ever reached.

units.zh: 至後周保定中，得古玉鬥於地中，以造尺律，其後牛弘以為不可，止用蘇綽鐵尺，至隋亦用之。
units.en: In the Baoding era of Later Zhou, an ancient jade bushel measure was unearthed and used to derive the foot-rule and pitch pipes; later Niu Hong rejected this method, and courts used only Su Chuo's iron foot-rule — a standard the Sui dynasty also adopted.
units.literal: In the Baoding era of Later Zhou, an ancient jade bushel measure was obtained from underground and used to make the foot-rule and pitch pipes; afterward Niu Hong held this impossible and used only Su Chuo's iron foot-rule, which the Sui also employed.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 至周顯德以黍定律，議者謂比唐樂高五律。
units.en: Under Later Zhou's Xiande reign, pitch was derived from millet grains; critics said the new standard stood five notes higher than Tang music.
units.literal: In Later Zhou's Xiande reign pitch was set by millet grains; debaters said it was five notes higher than Tang music.

units.zh: 宋初亦用王朴所制樂，時和峴以周顯德律音近哀思，乃依西京銅望臬、石尺重造十二管，取聲下王樸一律。
units.en: Early Song likewise used music composed by Wang Pu. He Xian argued that the Xiande pitch sounded too mournful, so he remade the twelve pipes according to the Western Capital's bronze pitch-standard and stone foot-rule, lowering the pitch one note below Wang Pu's standard.
units.literal: Early Song also used the music Wang Pu had made; at the time He Xian held that the Xiande pitch sounded too near grief and longing, so relying on the Western Capital's bronze pitch-standard and stone foot-rule he remade the twelve pipes, lowering the pitch one note below Wang Pu's.

units.zh: 景祐初，李照取黍累尺成律，以其聲猶高，更用太府布帛尺，遂下太常樂三律。
units.en: At the start of the Jingyou era, Li Zhao derived pitch pipes from a millet-based foot-rule; finding the tone still too high, he switched to the Grand Storehouse cloth-and-silk foot-rule and lowered Court of Imperial Sacrifices music by three notes.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, Li Zhao took millet to stack up the foot-rule and make pitch pipes; because the sound was still high, he used instead the Grand Storehouse cloth-and-silk foot-rule, and thus lowered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices music by three notes.

units.zh: 皇祐中，阮逸、胡瑗改造止下一律，或謂其聲弇鬱不和，依舊用王朴樂。
units.en: During Huangyou, Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan revised the standard again, lowering it by only one note; some complained that the tone was muffled and discordant, so the court reverted to Wang Pu's music.
units.literal: In Huangyou, Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan remade it, lowering only one note; some said the sound was muffled and gloomy and not harmonious, and they continued to use Wang Pu's music as before.

units.zh: 元豐間，楊傑參用李照鐘磬加四清聲，下王朴樂二律，以為新樂。
units.en: During Yuanfeng, Yang Jie adapted Li Zhao's bells and chimes, added four clear tones, lowered Wang Pu's standard by two notes, and established this as the new court music.
units.literal: In the Yuanfeng period, Yang Jie drew on Li Zhao's bells and chimes, added four clear tones, lowered Wang Pu's music by two notes, and made this the new music.

units.zh: 元祐間，範鎮又造新律，下李照樂一律，而未用。
units.en: During Yuanyou, Fan Zhen devised yet another pitch standard, one note lower than Li Zhao's, but it was never adopted.
units.literal: In the Yuanyou period, Fan Zhen again made new pitch pipes, lowering Li Zhao's music by one note, yet it was not adopted.

units.zh: 至崇甯間，魏漢津以範鎮知舊樂之高，無法以下之，乃以時君指節為尺，其所造鐘磐即今所用樂是也。
units.en: By the Chongning era, Wei Hanjin recognized that Fan Zhen knew the old music was too high yet had no practical way to lower it, so he took the reigning emperor's finger joints as the foot-rule; the bells and chimes he cast are the instruments in use today.
units.literal: By the Chongning period, Wei Hanjin, seeing that Fan Zhen knew the old music was too high and had no way to lower it, took the reigning lord's finger joints as the foot-rule; the bells and chimes he made are precisely the music used today.

units.zh: 然以王樸所制聲高，屢命改作，李照乙太府尺制律，人習舊聽疑於太重。
units.en: Because Wang Pu's music sounded too high, the court repeatedly ordered revisions. Li Zhao followed the Grand Storehouse foot-rule to set pitch, but listeners accustomed to the old standard thought the new tone too low and dull.
units.literal: Yet because the music Wang Pu had made sounded high, the court repeatedly ordered revisions; Li Zhao followed the Grand Storehouse foot-rule to make pitch pipes, but people accustomed to the old sound suspected it was too heavy.

units.zh: 其後范鎮等論樂，複用李照所用太府尺、即周、隋所用鐵尺，牛弘等以謂近古合宜者也。
units.en: Later Fan Zhen and others debated music and revived Li Zhao's Grand Storehouse foot-rule — the same iron standard used in Zhou and Sui times — which Niu Hong and others had regarded as close to antiquity and therefore appropriate.
units.literal: Afterward Fan Zhen and others debated music and again used the Grand Storehouse foot-rule that Li Zhao had used — that is, the iron foot-rule used by Zhou and Sui — which Niu Hong and others held to be near antiquity and fitting.

units.zh: 今取見有樂，以唐初開元錢校其分寸亦同，則漢津所用指尺殆與周、隋、唐所用之尺同矣。
units.en: When the music now in use is measured against early Tang Kaiyuan coins, the dimensions match as well; Wei Hanjin's finger-joint foot-rule was therefore probably the same standard used in Zhou, Sui, and Tang times.
units.literal: Now taking the music presently at hand and comparing its dimensions with early Tang Kaiyuan coins, they likewise agree; thus the finger-joint foot-rule Hanjin used was probably the same as the foot-rule used by Zhou, Sui, and Tang.

units.zh: 漢津用李照、範鎮之說，而恥同之，故用時君指節為尺，使眾人不敢輕議。
units.en: Hanjin drew on Li Zhao's and Fan Zhen's theories yet was unwilling to appear merely to follow them, so he took the reigning emperor's finger joints as the foot-rule so that critics would not dismiss his work lightly.
units.literal: Hanjin used the theories of Li Zhao and Fan Zhen yet was ashamed to be identical with them, so he used the reigning lord's finger joints as the foot-rule to keep the multitude from lightly criticizing.

units.zh: 其尺雖為詭說，其制乃與古同，而清濁高下皆適中，非出於法數之外私意妄為者也。
units.en: Although his foot-rule rested on a specious pretext, the resulting system matched antiquity, and its clear and muddy tones, high and low pitches, were all properly balanced — not the product of arbitrary private whim outside proper numerical standards.
units.literal: Although his foot-rule was a specious argument, its system was actually the same as antiquity, and clear and muddy, high and low, were all properly balanced — it was not something made by private whim outside the numerical laws.

units.zh: 蓋今之鐘磬雖崇寧之所制，亦周、隋、唐之樂也。
units.en: Thus today's bells and chimes, though cast in the Chongning era, are in substance the music of Zhou, Sui, and Tang.
units.literal: For today's bells and chimes, though made in Chongning, are also the music of Zhou, Sui, and Tang.

units.zh: 閱今所用樂律，聲調和平，無太高太下之失，可以久用。
units.en: Reviewing the pitch standard now in use, the tone is harmonious and balanced, neither too high nor too low, and may be retained for long-term use.
units.literal: Examining the pitch pipes now in use, the tone is harmonious and peaceful, without the fault of being too high or too low, and they may be used for a long time.

units.zh: 唯辰鐘、辰磬自昔數缺，宜補鑄辰鐘十五，辰磬二十一，通舊各為二十四虡。」
units.en: Only the chen bells and chen chimes have long been incomplete in number; the court should recast fifteen chen bells and twenty-one chen chimes so that, together with the old instruments, each set totals twenty-four stands."
units.literal: Only the chen bells and chen chimes have from old times been short in number; it is fitting to recast fifteen chen bells and twenty-one chen chimes, so that together with the old ones each set totals twenty-four stands."

units.zh: 上曰：「嘗觀宋人論樂，以為律主於人聲，不當泥於其器，要之在聲和而已。」
units.en: The emperor said: "I have read Song debates on music and believe that pitch standards should follow the human voice rather than cling rigidly to instruments; what matters above all is harmonious sound."
units.literal: The emperor said: "I have observed Song discussions of music and hold that pitch pipes take their authority from the human voice; one should not be rigidly bound to the instruments — what matters is simply that the sound be harmonious."

units.zh: 於是，命禮部符下南京，取宋舊工，更鑄辰鐘十有二。
units.en: He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to dispatch instructions to Nanjing, summon former Song craftsmen, and recast twelve chen bells.
units.literal: Thereupon he ordered the Ministry of Rites to send orders down to Nanjing, take old Song craftsmen, and recast twelve chen bells.

units.zh: 又以舊鐘姑洗、夷則皆高五律，無射高二律，別鑄以補之，乃協。
units.en: Because the old Guxian and Yize bells were each five notes too high and the Wushe bell two notes too high, the court cast replacements to fill the gaps, and the ensemble came into harmony.
units.literal: Moreover, because the old bells for Guxian and Yize were each five notes too high and Wushe two notes too high, separate bells were cast to supplement them, and then they were in harmony.

units.zh: 又琢辰磬各十有二，以其半少劣，擇其諧者而用之。
units.en: They also carved twelve chen chimes apiece; since roughly half were slightly inferior in tone, they selected the best-sounding pieces for use.
units.literal: They also carved twelve chen chimes each; because about half were slightly inferior, they selected the harmonious ones for use.

units.zh: 初，正隆間，海陵營太廟於汴，貞祐南遷，宣宗修之，以祔諸帝神主。
units.en: Earlier, during the Zhenglong era, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian. After the court moved south in the Zhenyou period, Emperor Xuanzong restored the temple to receive the spirit tablets of the former emperors.
units.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenglong period, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian; when the court moved south in the Zhenyou period, Emperor Xuanzong repaired it to enshrine the spirit tablets of the various emperors.

units.zh: 其地，故宋景靈宮之址也。
units.en: The site had been that of the Song dynasty's Jingling Palace.
units.literal: The site was the former location of the Song Jingling Palace.

units.zh: 掘其下，得編鐘十三，編磬八，皆刻「大晟」字。
units.en: Excavation below the site yielded thirteen chime-bells and eight chime-stones, all inscribed with the mark "Dasheng."
units.literal: When they dug beneath it, they obtained thirteen chime-bells and eight chime-stones, all inscribed with the characters "Dasheng."

units.zh: 時朝廷多故，禮器散亡，竟亦不能備也，
units.en: The court was then beset by many troubles, ritual vessels had been scattered and lost, and in the end the ensemble could not be made complete,
units.literal: At the time the court had many troubles and ritual vessels were scattered and lost, and in the end they could not be made complete either,

units.zh: 大定十一年，太常議：「按《唐會耍》舊制，南北郊宮縣用二十架，周、漢、魏、晉、宋、齊六朝及唐《開元》、宋《開寶禮》，其數皆同。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Dading, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "According to the Tang Huiyao, the palace ensemble for the southern and northern suburban sacrifices used twenty stands; Zhou, Han, Wei, Jin, Song, and Qi, as well as the Tang Kaiyuan Rites and Song Kaibao Rites, all prescribed the same number.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated: "According to the old system in the Tang Huiyao, the palace ensemble for the southern and northern suburban sacrifices used twenty stands; the six dynasties Zhou, Han, Wei, Jin, Song, and Qi, as well as the Tang Kaiyuan Rites and Song Kaibao Rites, all used the same number.

units.zh: 《宋會耍》用三十六架，《五禮新儀》用四十八架，其數多，似乎太侈。
units.en: The Song Huiyao prescribed thirty-six stands and the Wuli Xinyi forty-eight — numbers that seem excessively lavish by comparison.
units.literal: The Song Huiyao used thirty-six stands and the Wuli Xinyi used forty-eight stands — their numbers were greater and seem excessively lavish.

units.zh: 今擬《太常因革禮》，天子宮縣之樂三十六虡，宗廟與殿庭同，郊丘則二十虡，宜用宮縣二十架，登歌編鐘、編磬各一虡。
units.en: Following the Taichang Yingeli, the Son of Heaven's palace ensemble comprises thirty-six stands for ancestral temple and palace hall alike, while suburban mounds use twenty — the court should therefore employ a palace ensemble of twenty stands, with elevated song, chime-bells, and chime-stones each occupying one stand.
units.literal: Now following the Taichang Yingeli, the Son of Heaven's palace ensemble music has thirty-six stands; the ancestral temple and palace hall are the same, while suburban mounds use twenty stands — it is fitting to use a palace ensemble of twenty stands, with elevated song, chime-bells, and chime-stones each one stand.

units.zh: 又按《周禮大司樂》：'凡樂，圜鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太蔟為徵，姑洗為羽。
units.en: The Zhouli Director of Music also states: "In all music, the round bell serves as gong, huangzhong as jue, taicu as zhi, and guxian as yu."
units.literal: Moreover, according to the Zhouli Director of Music: "In all music, the round bell serves as gong, huangzhong as jue, taicu as zhi, and guxian as yu."

units.zh: 雷鼓、雷鞀、孤竹之管、雲和之琴瑟、雲門之舞，冬日至於地上之圜丘奏之，若樂六變，則天神皆降，可得而禮矣。
units.en: Thunder drums, thunder tambourines, solitary bamboo pipes, Yunhe zithers, and the Yunmen dance are performed at the round mound altar on the winter solstice; when the music undergoes six changes, the heavenly spirits descend and may be received in ritual.
units.literal: Thunder drums, thunder tambourines, solitary bamboo pipes, Yunhe zithers, and the Yunmen dance — at the winter solstice they are performed at the round mound altar on earth; if the music undergoes six changes, then the heavenly spirits all descend and may be received in ritual.

units.en: "Six changes" means six complete performances.
units.literal: "The six changes" means six completions.

units.en: Tang and Song followed the same practice.
units.literal: Tang and Song followed this.

units.zh: 蓋圜鐘，夾鐘也，用為宮者以上應房、心，有天帝明堂之象也。
units.en: The round bell is jiazhong; employed as gong, it corresponds above to the lodges Fang and Xin and evokes the Bright Hall of the Heavenly Emperor.
units.literal: For the round bell is jiazhong; used as gong, it corresponds above to the lodges Fang and Xin, having the image of the Heavenly Emperor's Bright Hall.

units.zh: 宮聲三奏，角徵羽各一奏，合陽之奇數，欲神聽之也。
units.en: The gong tone is played three times, while jue, zhi, and yu are each played once — an odd-numbered pattern of yang tones meant to draw the spirits' attention.
units.literal: The gong tone is played three times, jue, zhi, and yu each once — combining the odd numbers of yang, intending that the spirits should hear.

units.zh: 凡樂起于陽，至少陰而止，圜鐘自卯至申其數有六，故六變而樂止，則天神皆降，可得而禮也。
units.en: All music begins in yang and ends at least yin; the round bell spans from mao to shen in six stages, so after six changes the music ceases, the heavenly spirits descend, and ritual reception becomes possible.
units.literal: All music begins in yang and stops at least yin; the round bell from mao to shen has the number six, therefore with six changes the music stops, and then the heavenly spirits all descend and may be received in ritual.

units.zh: 樂曲之名，唐以'和'，宋以'安'，本朝定樂曲以'甯'為名，今止有太廟祫享樂曲，而郊祀樂曲未備。
units.en: Tang named ritual pieces with "He," Song with "An," and our dynasty adopted "Ning"; at present only the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint-offering pieces exist, while suburban sacrifice pieces are still incomplete.
units.literal: As for the names of musical pieces, Tang used "He," Song used "An," and our dynasty fixed musical pieces with "Ning" in the name; now there are only the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint-offering pieces, while suburban sacrifice pieces are not yet complete.

units.zh: 皇統九年拜天用《乾甯之曲》，今圜丘降神固可就用。
units.en: In the ninth year of Huangtong, the worship of Heaven used the "Qianning" piece, which can certainly be reused for the round mound's descent-of-spirit rite.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong, worship of Heaven used the "Qianning" piece; for the round mound's descent of the spirit it can certainly be used as is.

units.zh: 今太廟祫享，皇帝升降行止奏《昌甯之曲》，迎俎奏《豐甯之曲》，酌獻、舞出入奏《肅甯之曲》，飲福奏《福甯之曲》，宋《開寶禮》亦可就用。
units.en: At the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint offering, the emperor's ascent, descent, movement, and pauses are accompanied by "Changning"; welcoming the offering stand by "Fengning"; libation, offering, and dancers' entry and exit by "Suning"; and drinking the blessing by "Funing" — pieces that may likewise be drawn from the Song Kaibao Rites.
units.literal: Now for the Imperial Ancestral Temple joint offering, when the emperor ascends, descends, moves, or stops, the "Changning" piece is played; for welcoming the offering stand the "Fengning" piece; for libation, offering, and dancers entering and leaving the "Suning" piece; for drinking the blessing the "Funing" piece — the Song Kaibao Rites may also be used as is.

units.zh: 余有郊祀曲名，皇帝入中濆、奠玉幣、迎俎、酌獻、舞出入樂曲，宜皆以'寧'字制名。」
units.en: The remaining suburban sacrifice pieces — for the emperor's entry to the inner precinct, presentation of jade and silk, welcoming the offering stand, libation, and dancers' entry and exit — should all be named with "Ning.""
units.literal: As for the remaining suburban sacrifice piece names — when the emperor enters the inner precinct, presents jade and silk, welcomes the offering stand, pours libations, and dancers enter and leave — all should be named with the character "Ning.""

units.en: The emperor then ordered the Hanlin Academy to compose them.
units.literal: Thereupon he ordered the Hanlin Academy to compose them.

units.zh: 皇帝入中濆奏《昌甯之曲》，降神、送神奏《乾甯之曲》，昊天上帝奏《洪甯之曲》，皇地祇奏《坤甯之曲》，配位奏《永甯之曲》，飲福奏《福甯之曲》，升降、望燎、出入大小次，並與入中濆同，餘載儀注及樂章。
units.en: The emperor's entry to the inner precinct was accompanied by "Changning"; descent and sending off of the spirit by "Qianning"; August Heaven on High by "Hongning"; August Earth by "Kunning"; associated positions by "Yongning"; and drinking the blessing by "Funing"; ascent, descent, gazing at the burning, and movement between the great and small resting places followed the same piece as entry to the inner precinct. The remaining details are recorded in the ritual protocols and hymn texts.
units.literal: When the emperor entered the inner precinct, the "Changning" piece was played; for descent and sending off of the spirit, the "Qianning" piece; for August Heaven on High, the "Hongning" piece; for August Earth, the "Kunning" piece; for associated positions, the "Yongning" piece; for drinking the blessing, the "Funing" piece; for ascent, descent, gazing at the burning, and entering and leaving the great and small resting places, all were the same as entering the inner precinct; the rest are recorded in the ritual protocols and hymn texts.

units.zh: 又命太常議文武二舞所當先後，太常議：「按唐、宋郊廟之禮，並先文後武，本朝自行禘祫之禮亦然。
units.en: He also ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to decide the order of the civil and military dances. The Court reported: "Tang and Song suburban and temple rites both placed the civil dance before the military, and our dynasty's own di and xia offerings follow the same order.
units.literal: He also ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate which of the civil and military dances should come first. The Court deliberated: "According to Tang and Song suburban and temple rites, both put civil before military; our dynasty's own practice of the di and xia rites is likewise.

units.zh: 惟唐韋萬石建議謂先儒相傳，以揖讓得天下則先奏文，以征伐得天下則先奏武。
units.en: Only Wei Wanshi of Tang argued, following early Confucian tradition, that courts which gained the realm through yielding should play the civil dance first, while those that gained it through conquest should play the military dance first.
units.literal: Only Tang's Wei Wanshi proposed that the early Confucians transmitted that if one obtained the realm by yielding, civil was played first; if by military campaign, military was played first.

units.en: The court briefly followed his proposal but soon reverted.
units.literal: At the time they followed this, but soon changed it back.

units.zh: 其以《開元禮》先文後武為定。
units.en: They therefore fixed civil before military as prescribed in the Kaiyuan Rites.
units.literal: They took the Kaiyuan Rites' civil before military as fixed.

units.zh: 方丘如圜丘之儀，社稷則用登歌。」
units.en: The square mound follows the round mound's protocol, while the altars of soil and grain use elevated song alone."
units.literal: The square mound follows the round mound's protocol; the altars of soil and grain use elevated song."

units.en: Imperial Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 皇帝入門，宮縣以無射宮，升殿，登歌以夾鐘，皆奏《昌甯之曲》。
units.en: When the emperor entered the gate, the palace ensemble played in the wushe mode; when he ascended the hall, elevated song used jiazhong — both occasions accompanied by "Changning."
units.literal: When the emperor entered the gate, the palace ensemble used the wushe mode; when he ascended the hall, elevated song used jiazhong — both played the "Changning" piece.

units.zh: 迎神、送神奏《來甯之曲》，九成。
units.en: Welcoming and sending off the spirit were accompanied by the nine-part "Laining" piece.
units.literal: For welcoming and sending off the spirit, the "Laining" piece was played, in nine sections.

units.zh: 天德二年，晨稞畢，還小次，方奏迎神曲。
units.en: In the second year of Tiande, the spirit-welcoming piece was not played until after the morning offering had been completed and the emperor had returned to the small resting place.
units.literal: In the second year of Tiande, when the morning offering was finished and they returned to the small resting place, only then was the spirit-welcoming piece played.

units.zh: 大定十一年，朝享，奏依《開元》、《開寶禮》，至版位，即奏黃鐘宮三、大呂角二、太蔟徵二、應鐘羽二，曲詞皆同。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Dading, at the court offering, music followed the Kaiyuan and Kaibao Rites; upon reaching the spirit tablet, the ensemble played huangzhong gong three times, dalü jue twice, taicu zhi twice, and yingzhong yu twice, all to the same hymn text.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading, at the court offering, music followed the Kaiyuan and Kaibao Rites; upon reaching the spirit tablet position, huangzhong gong three times, dalü jue twice, taicu zhi twice, and yingzhong yu twice were played, all with the same text.

units.en: When the offering stand was brought forward, the court played "Fengning."
units.literal: When the offering stand was brought forward, the "Fengning" piece was played.

units.zh: 酌獻，宮縣奏無射《大元之曲》。
units.en: For the libation offering, the palace ensemble played the wushe-mode "Dayuan" piece.
units.literal: For pouring the libation, the palace ensemble played the wushe-mode "Dayuan" piece.

units.zh: 諸室之曲，德帝曰《大熙》，安帝曰《大安》，獻祖曰《大昭》，昭祖曰《大成》，景祖曰《大昌》，世祖曰《大武》，肅宗曰《大明》，穆宗曰《大章》，康宗曰《大康》，太祖曰《大定》，太宗曰《大惠》，熙宗曰《大同》，睿宗曰《大和》，昭德皇后廟曰《儀坤》，世宗曰《大鈞》，顯宗曰《大寧》，章宗曰《大隆》，宣宗曰《大慶》。
units.en: Each spirit chamber had its own piece: Emperor De, "Daxi"; Emperor An, "Da'an"; Ancestor Xian, "Dazhao"; Ancestor Zhao, "Dacheng"; Ancestor Jing, "Dachang"; Ancestor Shi, "Dawu"; Emperor Suzong, "Daming"; Emperor Muzong, "Dazhang"; Emperor Kangzong, "Dakang"; Emperor Taizu, "Dading"; Emperor Taizong, "Dahui"; Emperor Xizong, "Datong"; Emperor Ruizong, "Dahe"; the Temple of Empress Zhaode, "Yikun"; Emperor Shizong, "Dajun"; Emperor Xianzong, "Daning"; Emperor Zhangzong, "Dalong"; and Emperor Xuanzong, "Daqing."
units.literal: The pieces for the various chambers: Emperor De had "Daxi," Emperor An "Da'an," Ancestor Xian "Dazhao," Ancestor Zhao "Dacheng," Ancestor Jing "Dachang," Ancestor Shi "Dawu," Emperor Suzong "Daming," Emperor Muzong "Dazhang," Emperor Kangzong "Dakang," Emperor Taizu "Dading," Emperor Taizong "Dahui," Emperor Xizong "Datong," Emperor Ruizong "Dahe," the Temple of Empress Zhaode "Yikun," Emperor Shizong "Dajun," Emperor Xianzong "Daning," Emperor Zhangzong "Dalong," and Emperor Xuanzong "Daqing."

units.zh: 皇帝還版位及亞終獻，皆奏無射宮《肅甯之曲》。
units.en: When the emperor returned to the spirit tablet and for the secondary and final offerings, the wushe-mode "Suning" piece was played throughout.
units.literal: When the emperor returned to the spirit tablet position and for the secondary and final offerings, the wushe-mode "Suning" piece was played throughout.

units.zh: 飲福，登歌奏夾鐘宮《福甯之曲》。
units.en: For drinking the blessing, elevated song played the jiazhong-mode "Funing" piece.
units.literal: For drinking the blessing, elevated song played the jiazhong-mode "Funing" piece.

units.zh: 徹豆，奏《豐甯之曲》，皆用無射宮。
units.en: For removing the beans, the court played "Fengning," all in wushe mode.
units.literal: For removing the beans, the "Fengning" piece was played, all in wushe mode.

units.zh: 大定十二年制，祫禘時享有司攝事，初獻盥洗，奏無射宮《肅甯之曲》。
units.en: Under regulations issued in the twelfth year of Dading, when officials performed the joint di and xia offering by proxy, the wushe-mode "Suning" piece accompanied the first offering's hand-washing.
units.literal: By regulation of the twelfth year of Dading, at joint di and xia offerings when officials performed the rite by proxy, for the first offering's hand-washing the wushe-mode "Suning" piece was played.

units.zh: 升階，登歌奏夾鐘宮《嘉甯之曲》。
units.en: When ascending the steps, elevated song played the jiazhong-mode "Jianing" piece.
units.literal: When ascending the steps, elevated song played the jiazhong-mode "Jianing" piece.

units.en: Everything else followed the same order as when the emperor performed the rite in person.
units.literal: The remainder was all the same as when the emperor performed the rite in person.

units.zh: 其別廟昭德皇后、宣孝太子所用，並載儀注、樂章。
units.en: The music used at the separate temples of Empress Zhaode and Crown Prince Xuanxiao is recorded in the ritual protocols and hymn texts.
units.literal: What was used at the separate temples of Empress Zhaode and the Filial and Cultivated Crown Prince are all recorded in the ritual protocols and hymn texts.

units.zh: 舊制，太廟、皇考廟樂工各三十九人。
units.en: Under the old system, the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Imperial Father's Temple each employed thirty-nine musicians.
units.literal: Under the old system, the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Imperial Father's Temple each had thirty-nine musicians.

units.zh: 大定二十九年，升祔顯宗，有司以為：「宋之太廟、別廟，堂上樂各四十八人，今之樂工少十八人，擬令皇考廟舊樂工皆充兩廟堂上樂，以應前代九十六人之數。」
units.en: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, when Emperor Xianzong was elevated for joint enshrinement, officials reported: "Song's Imperial Ancestral Temple and separate temples each employed forty-eight hall musicians, whereas we are now eighteen short; we propose assigning all musicians from the Imperial Father's Temple to both temples' hall ensembles to match the former dynasty's total of ninety-six."
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, when Emperor Xianzong was elevated for joint enshrinement, the responsible officials held: "In Song's Imperial Ancestral Temple and separate temples, hall music each had forty-eight persons; today's musicians are eighteen fewer; it is proposed to have all the old musicians of the Imperial Father's Temple fill the hall music of both temples, to match the former dynasty's number of ninety-six."

units.zh: 尚書省議：「古樂工無定數。」
units.en: The Department of State Affairs deliberated: "In antiquity musicians had no fixed number."
units.literal: The Department of State Affairs deliberated: "In antiquity musicians had no fixed number."

units.zh: 遂奏太廟、別廟通以百人為定。
units.en: The court then fixed the combined musicians of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and separate temples at one hundred.
units.literal: They then memorialized that the Imperial Ancestral Temple and separate temples together should be fixed at one hundred persons.

units.zh: 明昌六年，創設宮縣，樂工一百五十六人。
units.en: In the sixth year of Mingchang, the court newly established a palace ensemble of one hundred fifty-six musicians.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Mingchang, the palace ensemble was newly established with one hundred fifty-six musicians.

units.zh: 承安三年，敕：「祭廟用教坊奏古樂，非禮也。
units.en: In the third year of Cheng'an, an edict declared: "Employing the Music Bureau to perform ancient music at temple sacrifices violates ritual propriety.
units.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an, an edict said: "Using the Music Bureau to perform ancient music at temple sacrifices is not ritual propriety.

units.zh: 其自今召百姓材美者，給以食直，教閱以待用。」
units.en: Henceforth the court should recruit talented commoners, provide them food allowances, and train them for future service."
units.literal: From now on summon commoners of outstanding talent, provide them food allowances, train and review them to await employment."

units.zh: 泰和元年，命宮縣樂工月給錢粟二貫石，遇正樂工闕，驗色收補。
units.en: In the first year of Taihe, palace ensemble musicians were granted two strings of cash and two shi of grain per month; when regular posts fell vacant, candidates were examined and recruited to fill them.
units.literal: In the first year of Taihe, palace ensemble musicians were ordered to receive two strings of cash and two shi of grain monthly; when regular musicians were short, they were examined and recruited to fill vacancies.

units.zh: 四年，尚書省奏：「宮縣樂工總用二百五十六人，而舊所設止百人，時或用之即以貼部教坊閱習。
units.en: In the fourth year, the Department of State Affairs reported: "The palace ensemble requires two hundred fifty-six musicians in all, yet the old establishment numbered only one hundred; when needed, musicians were temporarily drawn from the Music Bureau for training.
units.literal: In the fourth year, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: "The palace ensemble altogether requires two hundred fifty-six musicians, yet the old establishment was only one hundred; when needed they would temporarily attach musicians from the Music Bureau for review and practice.

units.zh: 自明昌間，以渤海教坊兼習，而又創設九十二人。
units.en: From the Mingchang period onward, the Bohai Music Bureau trained musicians jointly, and ninety-two additional posts were created.
units.literal: From the Mingchang period onward, the Bohai Music Bureau was used for joint practice, and ninety-two persons were also newly established.

units.zh: 且宮縣之樂行大禮乃始用之，若其數複闕，但前期遣漢人教坊及大興府樂人習之，亦可備用。」
units.en: Moreover, palace ensemble music is employed only for the greatest state rites; if numbers again fall short, the court can beforehand assign Han musicians from the Music Bureau and musicians of Daxing Prefecture to rehearse and stand ready."
units.literal: Moreover, palace ensemble music is used only when great rites are performed; if the number is again short, it is sufficient beforehand to send Han musicians from the Music Bureau and musicians of Daxing Prefecture to practice it, and they may also be made ready for use."

units.en: The court then abolished the newly created posts.
units.literal: An edict then abolished the newly established posts.

units.zh: 宣宗南遷，祔諸帝主於汴京太廟。
units.en: When Emperor Xuanzong moved south, he enshrined the spirit tablets of the former emperors in the Bianjing Imperial Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved south, he enshrined the spirit tablets of the various emperors in the Bianjing Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 禮官言：「祔享禮畢，車駕還宮，至承天門外，百官奉迎，宮縣奏《采茨》。」
units.en: Ritual officials reported: "After the joint enshrinement rite, when the imperial carriage returns to the palace and reaches the Chengtian Gate, the officials should welcome it while the palace ensemble plays 'Caici.'"
units.literal: The ritual officials said: "When the joint enshrinement rite is finished, the imperial carriage returns to the palace; upon reaching outside the Chengtian Gate, the hundred officials welcome it, and the palace ensemble plays 'Caici.'"

units.zh: 以樂虡未備，遂止用教坊樂。
units.en: Because the musical stands were incomplete, the court had to rely on Music Bureau music instead.
units.literal: Because the musical stands were not complete, they stopped at using Music Bureau music.

units.zh: 哀宗遷蔡，天興二年七月丁巳，太祖、太宗及後妃禦容至自汴京，奉安於乾元寺。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong moved to Cai, on a dingsi day in the seventh month of the second year of Tianxing, the imperial portraits of Taizu, Taizong, and the empresses arrived from Bianjing and were installed at Qianyuan Temple.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Cai, on the dingsi day of the seventh month of the second year of Tianxing, the imperial portraits of Taizu, Taizong, and the empresses arrived from Bianjing and were installed at Qianyuan Temple.

units.zh: 左宣徽使溫敦七十五奏當用樂。
units.en: The Left Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service Wendun Qishiwu memorialized that music should be performed.
units.literal: The Left Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service Wendun Qishiwu memorialized that music should be used.

units.en: The emperor said: "Music must come from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices — what can we do?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Music must come from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices — what is to be done?"

units.zh: 七十五曰：「市有優樂，可假用之。」
units.en: Qishiwu replied: "There are actors and musicians in the market who could be borrowed for the occasion."
units.literal: Qishiwu said: "There are actors and musicians in the market; they may be borrowed for use."

units.zh: 權左右司員外郎王鶚奏曰：「世俗之樂，豈可施於帝王之前？」
units.en: Acting Left and Right Department vice director Wang E objected: "How can vulgar popular music be performed before emperors?"
units.literal: Acting Left and Right Department vice director Wang E memorialized: "How can vulgar worldly music be performed before emperors?"

units.en: The proposal was dropped.
units.literal: They then stopped.

units.en: Names and numbers of musical instruments and dancers.
units.literal: Names and numbers of music and dance.

units.zh: 太廟登歌，鐘一虡，磬一虡，歌工四，籥二，塤二，篪二，笛二，巢笙二，和笙二，簫二，七星匏一，九耀匏一，閏餘匏一，搏拊二，柷一，敔一，麾一，一弦琴、三弦琴、五弦琴、七弦琴、九弦琴各二，瑟四。
units.en: For Imperial Ancestral Temple elevated song: one stand of bells, one stand of chimes, four singers, two yue pipes, two xun ocarinas, two chi flutes, two di flutes, two nest sheng, two he sheng, two xiao flutes, one seven-star gourd pipe, one nine-glory gourd pipe, one intercalary-remainder gourd pipe, two clappers, one sounding-wood, one scraper, one baton, two each of one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, and four se zithers.
units.literal: Imperial Ancestral Temple elevated song: bells one stand, chimes one stand, four singers, two yue pipes, two xun ocarinas, two chi flutes, two di flutes, two nest sheng, two he sheng, two xiao flutes, one seven-star gourd pipe, one nine-glory gourd pipe, one intercalary-remainder gourd pipe, two clappers, one sounding-wood, one scraper, one baton, one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers two each, four se zithers.

units.en: Separate temples used the same elevated-song ensemble.
units.literal: Separate temple elevated song was the same.

units.zh: 親祠則用金鐘、玉磬，攝祭則用編鐘、編磬。
units.en: When the emperor sacrificed in person, golden bells and jade chimes were used; when officials performed by proxy, chime-bells and chime-stones were used instead.
units.literal: When the emperor performed the sacrifice in person, golden bells and jade chimes were used; when officials performed by proxy, chime-bells and chime-stones were used.

units.zh: 宮縣樂三十六虡：編鐘十二虡，編磬十二虡，大鐘、穀鐘、特磬各四虡。
units.en: The palace ensemble comprised thirty-six stands: twelve of chime-bells, twelve of chime-stones, and four each of great bells, grain bells, and special chimes.
units.literal: Palace ensemble music had thirty-six stands: chime-bells twelve stands, chime-stones twelve stands, great bells, grain bells, and special chimes four stands each.

units.zh: 建鼓、應鼓、鞞鼓各四，路鼓二，路鞀二，晉鼓一，巢笙、竽笙各十，簫十，籥十，篪十，笛十，塤八，一弦琴三，三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴各六，瑟十二，柷一，敔一，麾一。
units.en: It also included four each of establishment drums, response drums, and leather drums; two road drums and two road tambourines; one Jin drum; ten each of nest sheng and yu sheng; ten xiao, ten yue, ten chi, ten di, and eight xun; three one-string zithers and six each of three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers; twelve se zithers; and one sounding-wood, one scraper, and one baton.
units.literal: Establishment drums, response drums, and leather drums four each; road drums two, road tambourines two, Jin drum one; nest sheng and yu sheng ten each; xiao ten, yue ten, chi ten, di ten, xun eight; one-string zither three, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers six each; se twelve; sounding-wood one, scraper one, baton one.

units.zh: 文舞所執籥、翟各六十四，武舞所執硃幹、玉戚各六十四，引舞所執旌二，纛二，牙杖二，單鞀二，單鐸二，雙鐸二，金鐃二，金錞二，金鉦二，相鼓二，雅鼓二。
units.en: Civil dancers carried sixty-four yue pipes and sixty-four pheasant-feather staffs apiece; military dancers carried sixty-four vermilion staffs and sixty-four jade axes apiece; leading dancers carried two banners, two great banners, two ivory staffs, two single tambourines, two single bells, two double bells, two golden nao, two golden chun, two golden zheng, two xiang drums, and two ya drums.
units.literal: The civil dance held yue pipes and pheasant-feather staffs sixty-four each; the military dance held vermilion staffs and jade axes sixty-four each; the leading dancers held banners two, great banners two, ivory staffs two, single tambourines two, single bells two, double bells two, golden nao two, golden chun two, golden zheng two, xiang drums two, and ya drums two.

units.zh: 有司攝祭，宮縣二十虡：編鐘四，編磬四，辰鐘十二。
units.en: When officials performed sacrifices by proxy, the palace ensemble used twenty stands: four of chime-bells, four of chime-stones, and twelve chen bells.
units.literal: When officials performed the sacrifice by proxy, the palace ensemble had twenty stands: chime-bells four, chime-stones four, chen bells twelve.

units.zh: 建鼓四，路鼓四，路鞀二，晉鼓一，巢笙、竽笙、簫、塤、篪、笛各八，一弦琴三，三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴各六，瑟八，柷、敔各一，麾一。
units.en: The proxy ensemble also included four establishment drums, four road drums, two road tambourines, one Jin drum, eight each of nest sheng, yu sheng, xiao, xun, chi, and di, three one-string zithers, six each of three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers, eight se zithers, one sounding-wood, one scraper, and one baton.
units.literal: Establishment drums four, road drums four, road tambourines two, Jin drum one; nest sheng, yu sheng, xiao, xun, chi, and di eight each; one-string zither three, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers six each; se eight; sounding-wood and scraper one each; baton one.

units.zh: 登歌及二舞引舞所執與親祠同。
units.en: Elevated song and the implements carried by the leading dancers of the two ritual dances were the same as for sacrifices performed by the emperor in person.
units.literal: Elevated song and what the two dances' leading dancers held were the same as when the emperor sacrificed in person.

units.en: The Emperor Receives the Seal and Regalia.
units.literal: The emperor received the seal and regalia.

units.zh: 前期，大樂令與協律郎設樂縣於殿廷。
units.en: Beforehand, the Director of Great Music and the Pitch-Regulating Gentleman set up the musical stands in the palace courtyard.
units.literal: Beforehand, the Director of Great Music and the Pitch-Regulating Gentleman set up the musical stands in the palace courtyard.

units.zh: 又設舉麾位二，一於殿西階，一于樂縣西北。
units.en: They also established two baton-raising positions, one at the hall's western steps and one northwest of the musical stands.
units.literal: They also set up two baton-raising positions, one at the western steps of the hall and one northwest of the musical stands.

units.en: They also set up the elevated-song music frame inside the hall.
units.literal: They also set up the elevated-song music frame on the hall.

units.en: On the appointed day, the attendant-in-chief reported: "The outer preparations are complete."
units.literal: On the day, the attendant-in-chief reported: "The outer preparations are complete."

units.zh: 宮縣樂作，皇帝乃出，即坐，樂止。
units.en: The palace ensemble began to play; the emperor then emerged, took his seat, and the music ceased.
units.literal: The palace ensemble music began; the emperor then came forth, took his seat, and the music stopped.

units.zh: 奉寶入門，樂作，置褥位上，樂止。
units.en: When the regalia was brought through the gate, music began; once it was placed on the cushion seat, the music stopped.
units.literal: When the regalia was brought in through the gate, music began; it was placed on the cushion seat, and music stopped.

units.zh: 初引時宮縣樂作，至位立定，樂止。
units.en: When the regalia was first led forward, the palace ensemble played; once it reached its position and stood still, the music stopped.
units.literal: At the first leading forth, palace ensemble music began; upon reaching the position and standing fixed, music stopped.

units.zh: 寶初行，樂作，至御前置訖，樂止。
units.en: When the regalia first moved forward, music began; once it had been set before the imperial seat, the music stopped.
units.literal: When the regalia first moved, music began; upon reaching completion before the imperial seat, music stopped.

units.zh: 皇帝受寶訖，樂作，侍中奏：「稱賀。」
units.en: After the emperor had received the regalia, music began and the attendant-in-chief announced: "Offer congratulations."
units.literal: When the emperor had finished receiving the regalia, music began; the attendant-in-chief reported: "Offer congratulations."

units.en: The music then stopped.
units.literal: Music stopped.

units.zh: 皇太子升殿，登歌樂作，復位，樂止。
units.en: The crown prince ascended the hall to elevated song; when he returned to his place, the music stopped.
units.literal: The crown prince ascended the hall; elevated song music began; he returned to his place, and music stopped.

units.en: The attendant-in-chief reported: "The rite is complete."
units.literal: The attendant-in-chief reported: "The rite is finished."

units.zh: 宮縣樂作，皇帝還幕次，樂止。
units.en: The palace ensemble played as the emperor returned to the curtain pavilion, and the music stopped.
units.literal: Palace ensemble music began; the emperor returned to the curtain pavilion, and music stopped.

units.en: Announcing Amnesty from the Imperial Tower.
units.literal: Announcing amnesty from the imperial tower.

units.zh: 前期，大樂署設宮縣於樓下，又設鼓一于宮縣之左。
units.en: Beforehand, the Office of Great Music set up the palace ensemble below the tower and placed one drum to its left.
units.literal: Beforehand, the Office of Great Music set up the palace ensemble below the tower and also set up one drum to the left of the palace ensemble.

units.zh: 至日，金雞初立，大樂署擊鼓，立訖，鼓止。
units.en: On the appointed day, when the golden rooster was first raised, the Office of Great Music struck the drum; once the raising was complete, the drumming stopped.
units.literal: On the day, when the golden rooster was first raised, the Office of Great Music struck the drum; when the raising was finished, the drum stopped.

units.en: The attendant-in-chief reported: "The outer preparations are complete."
units.literal: The attendant-in-chief reported: "The outer preparations are complete."

units.zh: 大樂令撞黃鐘之鐘，右五鐘皆應，《昌甯之樂》作，皇帝乃出。
units.en: The Director of Great Music struck the huangzhong bell; the five bells to the right answered in turn; "Changning" began to play, and the emperor emerged.
units.literal: The Director of Great Music struck the huangzhong bell; the five bells to the right all responded; the "Changning" music began, and the emperor then came forth.

units.zh: 宣讀訖，百官舞蹈，禮畢，大樂令撞蕤賓之鐘，左五鐘皆應，《昌甯之樂》作，皇帝降座，樂止。
units.en: After the amnesty had been read aloud, the officials performed the ritual dance. When the rite was complete, the Director of Great Music struck the ruibin bell; the five bells to the left answered; "Changning" played again as the emperor left his seat, and the music stopped.
units.literal: When the proclamation reading was finished, the hundred officials danced; when the rite was complete, the Director of Great Music struck the ruibin bell; the five bells to the left all responded; the "Changning" music began; the emperor descended from the seat, and music stopped.

units.zh: 凡皇帝出入升降及分班合班，皆樂作，坐、立定乃止。
units.en: Whenever the emperor entered, exited, ascended, descended, or formed and re-formed ranks, music played and ceased only once he was seated or standing still.
units.literal: Whenever the emperor entered, exited, ascended, descended, or formed and re-formed ranks, music always began and stopped only when he was seated or standing fixed.

units.zh: 其冊命中宮、皇太子、太孫，受外國使賀。
units.en: The same applied to investitures of the empress, crown prince, and imperial great-grandson, and to receptions of congratulations from foreign envoys.
units.literal: For investiture of the empress, crown prince, and imperial great-grandson, and for receiving congratulations from foreign envoys —

units.en: Banquets for foreign envoys all employed the palace ensemble.
units.literal: banquets for foreign envoys all used the palace ensemble.

units.zh: 元日、聖誕稱賀，曲宴外國使，則教坊奏之。
units.en: On New Year's Day, imperial birthday congratulations, and informal banquets for foreign envoys, the Music Bureau performed instead.
units.literal: On New Year's Day and the imperial birthday congratulations, and informal banquets for foreign envoys, the Music Bureau performed.

units.en: The names of their instruments and pieces have not been preserved.
units.literal: Their instrument names and piece titles are not transmitted.

units.zh: 皇統二年宰臣奏：「自古並無伶人赴朝參之例，所有教坊人員只宜聽候宣喚，不合同百寮赴起居。」
units.en: In the second year of Huangtong the chief ministers reported: "Never in antiquity have actors attended court audience; Music Bureau personnel should await summons only and should not join the hundred officials at the imperial levee."
units.literal: In the second year of Huangtong the chief ministers memorialized: "From antiquity there has never been a precedent for actors attending court audience; all Music Bureau personnel should only await summons and should not join the hundred officials in attending the imperial levee."

units.en: The court approved.
units.literal: The court approved.

units.zh: 章宗明昌二年十一月甲寅，禁伶人不得以歷代帝王為戲及稱萬歲者，以不應為事重法科。
units.en: On a jiayin day in the eleventh month of the second year of Mingchang, Emperor Zhangzong forbade actors from portraying emperors of past dynasties in jest or shouting "ten thousand years," imposing heavy penalties under the statute for impermissible conduct.
units.literal: On the jiayin day of the eleventh month of the second year of Mingchang under Emperor Zhangzong, actors were forbidden to make sport of emperors of successive dynasties or to shout "ten thousand years"; this was punished under the statute for impermissible conduct with heavy penalties.

units.zh: 泰和初，有司又奏太常工人數少，即以渤海，漢人教坊及大興府樂人兼習以備用。
units.en: Early in the Taihe era, officials again reported that Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians were too few, and assigned musicians from the Bohai and Han Music Bureaus and from Daxing Prefecture to train jointly as reserves.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, the responsible officials again memorialized that Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians were few in number, and so musicians from the Bohai and Han Music Bureaus and musicians of Daxing Prefecture were assigned joint practice to stand ready for use.

units.en: Wind-and-Drum Music.
units.literal: Wind-and-drum music.

units.en: This was music performed on horseback.
units.literal: This is music on horseback.

units.zh: 天子鼓吹、橫吹各有前、後部，部又各分二節。
units.en: The Son of Heaven's wind music and transverse wind music each had front and rear sections, and each section was further divided into two parts.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's wind music and transverse wind music each had front and rear sections, and each section was further divided into two parts.

units.zh: 金初用遼故物，其後雜用宋儀。
units.en: Early Jin used Liao legacy equipment; later the court blended in Song protocols as well.
units.literal: Early Jin used Liao legacy items; afterward they mixed in Song protocols.

units.zh: 海陵遷燕及大定十一年鹵簿，皆分鼓吹為四節，其他行幸惟用兩部而已。
units.en: When Prince Hailing moved the capital to Yan and in the eleventh year of Dading for the full imperial procession, wind music was divided into four sections; on other tours only two sections were used.
units.literal: When Prince Hailing moved to Yan and in the eleventh year of Dading for the imperial procession, wind music was all divided into four parts; on other tours only two sections were used.

units.literal: Great drums one hundred twenty, long-sounding pipes one hundred twenty.
